ost.outcome: A user who leaves AI work running at night finds it carried through by morning, as work stopped at the usage limit or by an error resumes on its own once it can, and the next work starts when one ends.

opportunities.opportunity: Once the usage limit lifts, the work resumes on its own.

children.opportunity: Not only at the usage limit: when an error happens, retry.
Change how many times it retries.

solutions.solution: The user starts one work from Claude Code, with its folder, its prompt, and the tools it may use, and leaves; it runs headless through `claude -p`, and on the usage limit or any error it is asked to go on in the same session after a wait of 5, 10, 20, then 60 minutes, up to 7 retries by default or as many as the user says, so that by morning the work is done, or recorded as failed, with its log.
assumptions: A run succeeded exactly when `claude -p --output-format json` exits 0 and its result has `is_error` false; the usage limit and other errors show as anything else.
`claude -p --resume <session_id>` goes on from where the failed run stopped.
Asking again while the limit holds only fails again, and does no harm.
Waits of 5, 10, 20, then 60 minutes, 7 times, span the 5-hour limit, and resume within an hour of its lifting.
Unit tests with a stand-in for `claude` that returns what the real one does show that it works, so the user need not try it on a real night.

opportunities.opportunity: When all of it is done, start the next work.
Put any number of works in the queue.
Start at a given time, or start right away.
Say how many run at once; three by default.

decisions: The user gives the purpose and intent; how the work goes on is the orchestrator's to decide.
The work runs from outside Claude Code: a command starts `claude -p` and retries it, as Claude Code's own continue at the usage limit is unstable; no keys are sent into an interactive session.
It retries on any error, not only the usage limit.
Success is exit code 0 with `is_error` false in the JSON result; anything else is retried, as an exit code alone has shown 0 on a rate limit (anthropics/claude-code#79500).
A retry goes on in the same session by `--resume <session_id>`.
Waits between retries: 5, 10, 20 minutes, then 60 minutes each; 7 retries by default (275 minutes in all); the count can be changed.
A work whose retries run out is recorded as failed.
Each work names its folder and the tools it may use, and leaves its state and log.
The first slice is one work that retries; the queue, the next work's start, the start time, and the number at once come after, one at a time.

Later, once the queue comes: it holds any number of works, the next starts when one ends, works start at a given time or right away, 3 run at once by default and the number can be changed, a work whose retries run out lets the queue move on, and the queue lives in a file so that a stopped command picks up where it was.
Python, standard library alone, with unit tests; the user doesn't try it, as the tests show it works.
A new plugin, overnight, with README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, a marketplace entry, and a line in the repository's README.
The user doesn't see the README once it's made.

The `overnight` command sits in the plugin's bin/, which Claude Code puts on the PATH of its own shell, so the user starts a work from Claude Code (such as `! overnight ...`) with no setup; the command runs apart from the session, so closing Claude Code doesn't stop it. A plain terminal outside Claude Code doesn't get bin/ on its PATH.

The README's links to LICENSE and CHANGELOG and its install line hold once the first task puts them and the marketplace entry in place; its order follows the readme template, and its top status says it's in development, so it takes no remedy after its first judged Round.
The English check's settings don't change; what it finds is mended in the text.

A retry with no conversation to go on in, as no earlier run named one, gives the prompt again, as nothing was done yet; a resume that names no conversation leaves the one it resumed for the next retry. The README's "No" to starting over stays true, so neither takes a remedy.
The tests check the retry after a resume that finds no conversation, test each case once, and check that each retry resumes the conversation with continue.
The user had both points that the Rounds left mended: no test compares minutes read from the real clock, and the command's test takes --retries 0 as the least it accepts.
